event.reason.no_time: There is no time before the crew rotation.
tablet.no_energy: No energy today: systems run at minimum.
tablet.effect.workshop_ready: Ready to repair and send the rover.
tablet.effect.sheltered: No production: you are in the shelter.
tablet.budget.wasted: The battery is full: {valor} will be lost. Give it to a module.
tablet.needs_workshop.repair: The workshop needs {min} energy or the repair will not happen.
tablet.needs_workshop.rover: The workshop needs {min} energy or the rover cannot leave.

sun.event_note: Your first storm will be this real event.
storm.origin.live: Based on a real event from {fecha}, recorded by NASA DONKI.
storm.origin.real: Based on a real event from {fecha}, recorded by NASA DONKI.
scene.hint: Tap a base module to give it energy
hud.days_strip: The 30 days of the mission; dark ones are the lunar night
hud.night_now: Lunar night: {dias} days without sun left
module.recycler.what: Cleans the air and recycles water.
module.greenhouse.what: Grows food. Uses a little water.
module.workshop.what: Repairs modules and sends the rover. It also powers the antenna: with it, Earth warns you about storms.
tablet.budget.left: {quedan} of {total} left to share. What you do not use is stored in the battery.
tablet.budget.none: You shared out all the energy.
coach.welcome.title: You are the commander of this base
coach.welcome.crew: You look after {personas} astronauts on the Moon.
coach.welcome.energy: Your job: share the energy from the Sun.
coach.welcome.night: On day {noche} the lunar night arrives: {duracion} days with no Sun. Save battery before it.
coach.welcome.lose: If air or food reach 0, the mission is cancelled and everyone returns to Earth.
coach.pick_recycler: Tap the Recycler. It gives us air and water.
coach.pick_greenhouse: Nice! Now tap the Greenhouse: that is where food grows.
coach.power_greenhouse: Fill the Greenhouse to {invernadero} or more. Without it, food drops {comida} every day.
coach.verdict: This stamp shows how the base will be tomorrow. What you do not share is saved in the battery.
coach.execute: The stamp shows how we will be tomorrow. Press "Play the day".
coach.night: Night arrives in {faltan} days. Save battery!
help.title: How to play
help.goal: Your mission: get the {personas} people on the base safely to day {dias}.
help.step1: Tap a module and decide how much energy to give it.
help.step2: Check the notice: it tells you how the base will be tomorrow.
help.step3: Press "Play the day". What you do not spend is saved in the battery.
help.life_support: Air and water. Drops {aire} every day. The Recycler raises it. At 0 the mission is cancelled.
help.food: Drops {comida} every day. The Greenhouse raises it. At 0 the mission is cancelled.
help.battery: Stored energy. At night it is all you have.
help.dose: Radiation is invisible energy from the Sun that harms the body. It is measured in mSv. If it fills the circle, the mission is cancelled.
help.night: From day {noche} on, {duracion} days with no Sun. Arrive with a full battery.
help.workshop: Repairs modules, sends the rover and powers the antenna that warns of storms. Only works with {taller} or more.
help.storm: In a solar storm you choose: shelter (almost no radiation, but less production) or keep working (more radiation).
event.storm.title: Solar storm incoming!
event.storm.text: The Sun launched a {tipo}{detalle}: a cloud of particles that harms the body. It arrives in a few hours. What do we do?
event.breakdown.title: Breakdown: {modulo}
event.breakdown.text: A part of {modulo} broke. It will produce nothing until you repair it.
event.ice.title: Ice detected
event.ice.text: We found ice in a nearby crater. Ice is water: for drinking and for making air.
event.night_warning.title: The lunar night is coming
event.night_warning.text: Soon the Sun will hide behind the crater. No Sun means no new energy. Charge the battery now!
event.effect.rover_gain_maybe: Tomorrow (or the day after): +{valor} life support
debrief.abort: The crew returned safely to Earth in the emergency ship.
debrief.win.stars1: You made it, but something was very tight. Save more battery before the night.
debrief.win.stars2: Good job! You saved energy for the night and nobody was in serious danger.
debrief.win.stars3: Perfect mission! You always had energy to spare. That is how a real commander plans.
debrief.cause.life_support: Air and water ran out. The Recycler needed more energy.
debrief.cause.food: Food ran out. The Greenhouse needs energy almost every day.
debrief.cause.radiation: The crew got too much radiation. The shelter and the Shielding keep it low.
debrief.night_long: The night lasted longer than your battery. Without the Sun, you can only use what you saved before.
debrief.decisive.life_support: It all started on day {dia}, when air and water dropped below 25.
debrief.decisive.food: It all started on day {dia}, when food dropped below 25.
debrief.decisive.radiation: It all started on day {dia}, when radiation passed 70% of the limit.
debrief.rewind: Go back to day {dia} and try again
debrief.chart.title: Your mission, day by day
debrief.chart.aria: Chart of life support, food, battery and radiation during the mission. Use the button below to see the data as a table.
debrief.share.win: I kept a base running for {dias} days at the Moon's south pole with {estrellas} in Shackleton: Night Shift.
debrief.share.loss: I reached day {dia} running a base at the Moon's south pole in Shackleton: Night Shift. Next time I make it to 30!
menu.pitch: You are in charge of {personas} astronauts for {dias} days on a science expedition.
menu.mission.cadete.what: Your first mission. With room to learn.
menu.mission.comandante.what: The full challenge. Every decision counts.
crew.title: Meet your crew
crew.valeria.name: Valeria Andrade
crew.valeria.quote: Every drop of water is recycled. If the Recycler stops, we all feel it when we breathe.
crew.mateo.name: Mateo Quishpe
crew.mateo.quote: If the greenhouse runs out of light, I run out of lettuce.
crew.amaru.name: Amaru Tene
crew.amaru.quote: When the Sun gets angry, we go to the shelter. No arguing.
crew.lucia.name: Lucía Herrera
crew.lucia.quote: Give me ten energy in the workshop and I will fix anything. Even the rover.
title.subtitle: NIGHT SHIFT
title.pitch: You are in charge of 4 astronauts for thirty days on a science expedition.
title.team: Team Halo Sur · NASA Space Apps 2026 · Sangolquí, Ecuador
crew.hint: Tap an astronaut to meet them.
sun.compact: Sun active today: {tipo} on {fecha} (level {nivel}) · NASA DONKI
crew.valeria.good: The air is clean and the water flows. Good job, {nombre}!
crew.valeria.worried: {nombre}, air and water are dropping. The Recycler needs more energy.
crew.mateo.good: The lettuce is growing happily, {nombre}! Salad for everyone.
crew.mateo.worried: {nombre}, the pantry is emptying. The Greenhouse needs energy.
crew.amaru.good: Radiation is under control, {nombre}. I keep watching the Sun.
crew.amaru.worried: {nombre}, we have taken a lot of radiation. More Shielding, please.
crew.lucia.good: Everything works, {nombre}. My tools can rest.
crew.lucia.worried: {nombre}, something is failing or the battery is very low. I am on it.
debrief.voice.life_support: We ran out of air and water, {nombre}!
debrief.voice.win: We did it, {nombre}! Thirty days on the Moon.
debrief.tip.life_support: give the Recycler more energy every day, and save battery before the night.
debrief.tip.food: don't leave the Greenhouse without energy: plants need it almost every day.
debrief.tip.radiation: during storms, everyone to the shelter; and power the Shielding.
warn.title: Message from Earth: solar storm in {dias} days
warn.title_one: Message from Earth: solar storm tomorrow
warn.advice: Charge the battery and get the Shield ready.
help.antenna: The Workshop also powers the antenna. With it, Earth warns you about storms {aviso} days ahead. A signal takes just over 1 second to reach the Moon; to Mars, between 4 and 24 minutes!
sources.button: Where does the data come from?
sources.title: Where does the data come from?
sources.intro: This game mixes real NASA data with made-up parts so it is playable. Here is which is which.
sources.error: We could not load the list right now. Please try again in a bit.
science.title: Real science
science.iss: On the Space Station, a NASA instrument measured about {dosis} micrograys of radiation per day (April 2022 average).
science.iss_hint: The gray is the unit that measures the radiation a body absorbs.
coach.welcome.goal: Last {dias} days and we all go home.
coach.greenhouse: Now the Greenhouse: give it {invernadero}. It is our food!
loading.tip.1: Save battery before the lunar night arrives.
loading.tip.2: If a solar storm is coming, send the crew to the shelter.
loading.tip.3: Tap a module of the base to give it energy.
loading.tip.4: Energy you don’t hand out is stored in the battery.
loading.tip.5: The Recycler makes air and water. The Greenhouse makes food.
loading.tip.6: If something goes wrong, the report lets you go back to an earlier day.
onb.1.title: Your mission
onb.1.a: You are in charge of {personas} astronauts for {dias} days on a science expedition.
onb.1.b: Keep them safe until the relief ship arrives.
onb.2.title: Energy
onb.2.a: The Sun charges your battery. Each day you share that energy among the modules.
onb.2.b: Energy you don't use is saved in the battery, until it is full.
onb.3.title: Today's plan
onb.3.a: Each day you choose how much energy each module gets, then press "Pass the day".
onb.3.b: You can tap the modules on the base or use the panel.
onb.4.title: What is coming
onb.4.night.name: Lunar night
onb.4.night.text: Several days without Sun. Fill your battery first.
onb.4.storm.name: Solar storms
onb.4.storm.text: Dangerous particles. Decide if you go to the shelter.
onb.4.repair.name: Breakdowns
onb.4.repair.text: Something breaks. Fix it with the Workshop.
onb.4.ice.name: Ice
onb.5.title: How you win and lose
onb.5.win: You win: you reach day {dias} with the whole crew safe.
onb.5.lose: You lose if air and water run out, food runs out, or radiation passes the limit.
onb.5.safe: If you lose, the crew returns safely in the emergency ship.
onb.6.title: Your crew
onb.6.a: Each one looks after a module. Their faces tell you how things are going.
coach.hint_day2: Here you see today's energy: Sun, battery and what you can share.
coach.hint_day3: This stamp tells you how the base will be tomorrow.
eflow.tip.sun: Energy the panels make today from sunlight.
eflow.tip.no_sun: It is night: the panels make no energy. You only have your battery.
eflow.tip.battery: It saves the energy you do not use. If it fills up, the extra is lost.
eflow.tip.spend: Sun + battery − {base} the base uses. This is what you share today. These are game energy units.
eflow.base: The base uses {base} just by being switched on.
board.after_today: Air & water {aire} · Food {comida} · Battery will be {bateria}
sunfc.title: Sun forecast: next days
repair.title: {modulo} is broken
repair.need: You need {min} free energy to repair.
repair.in_progress: Ready when the day ends. Lucía is on her way.
info.storm.1: The Sun threw out very fast particles.
info.storm.2: On Earth, the atmosphere protects us.
info.storm.3: On the Moon, nothing slows them down.
info.storm.alt: Drawing: the Sun sends particles (level {nivel} of 4) toward the lunar base. On Earth a shield bends them away; on the Moon nothing stops them.
info.night.1: At the south pole the Sun always hangs very low.
info.night.2: When it slips behind the mountains, your base sits in shadow for days.
info.night.alt: Drawing: the Sun sinks and hides behind the mountains; the base falls into shadow.
info.breakdown.2: Fixing it costs {min} energy from the Workshop.
info.breakdown.alt: Drawing: the broken part of {modulo} throws sparks. Fixing it costs {min} energy from the Workshop.
info.ice.1: Some craters never get any light.
info.ice.2: There, water stayed frozen for millions of years.
info.ice.alt: Drawing: a crater in permanent shadow with ice at the bottom and the rover on the rim.
info.dust.1: Moon dust is fine and sticks to everything.
info.dust.2: It covers the panels, so they give less energy.
info.dust.alt: Drawing: dust stuck on a solar panel blocks the light; a rover cleans it with a brush.
